mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 YoY growth is below -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO falls for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 5-year averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (i.e., more people in the labor force but unemployment rising) indicates weak job quality or underemployment, which reduces consumer purchasing power and drags on corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market normalization with rising underemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE also rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumer spending intentions, which negatively impacts corporate sales and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average for three straight months.
